answer: Nothing travels faster than light, and that single law makes geography expensive. A verifier in each region flings a nonce at a wallet and demands an instant reply; the round-trip delay pins the machine to that district, the way an echo comes back late when you shout across a canyon. A clone can copy a private key onto a thousand laptops, but it cannot be in two districts before the clock window closes, so one wallet earns one stamp in one place. Cloning then means renting real servers inside every wharf of every region, a per-region bill no script can dodge.
